subject.title: Rebrand text-substitution filter on tool-call arguments silently misroutes file ops

question: Should plugin text transforms be allowed to rewrite executable/tool/path-bearing strings, and which core boundary should enforce that policy before this issue is fixed?
rationale: Current main and docs make text transforms a public plugin/provider/CLI contract, so disabling, path-scoping, or adding an opt-out changes compatibility and upgrade behavior beyond a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Protect executable arguments by default
options.body: Disable or path-scope transforms before tool execution/file operations while keeping cosmetic display transforms, then require focused regression and live dual-directory proof.

options.title: Keep transforms broad and document hooks
options.body: Preserve current transform semantics and tell plugins to use before_tool_call or another explicit hook for path-sensitive policies, accepting the reported split-state risk.

options.title: Rebase and review the fork PR
options.body: Use the linked fork PR as candidate implementation, but resolve its conflict, path heuristic, and env-var compatibility before merge.

recommendation.title: Protect executable arguments by default
recommendation.body: Disable or path-scope transforms before tool execution/file operations while keeping cosmetic display transforms, then require focused regression and live dual-directory proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current text-transform helper, tool-call argument coverage, docs, and provider/CLI wiring are all blamed to the same recent commit attributed to this area.
